ev.q: estimated MCV1 coverage increased globally from 72% to 86%
the number of reported cases decreased 59%, from 853,479 in 2000 to 353,236 in 2018
measles incidence decreased 66%, from 145 to 49 cases per million population
estimated measles deaths decreased 73%, from 535,600 to 142,300
Globally, 118 (61%) countries achieved ≥90% MCV1 coverage in 2018
By the end of 2018, 82 (42%) countries had been verified as having eliminated measles
the number of measles cases in 2018 increased 167% globally compared with 2016
compared with no measles vaccination, measles vaccination prevented an estimated 23.2 million deaths globally
describes progress toward WHA milestones and regional measles elimination during 2000–2018
Countries report the number of incident measles cases to WHO and UNICEF annually
During 2000–2018, annual reported measles incidence decreased 66%

methods_quotes.q: WHO and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) use data from administrative records and vaccination coverage surveys reported annually
A previously described model for estimating measles cases and deaths was updated with new measles vaccination coverage data
For countries with anomalous estimates in previous iterations, the model was modified slightly to generate mortality estimates consistent with observed case data.
Error bars represent upper and lower 95% confidence limits around the point estimate.
Deaths prevented by vaccination are estimated by the area between estimated deaths with vaccination and those without vaccination
The discarded case rate is used to measure the sensitivity of measles surveillance.
